chunks: When Our clear messages are recited to them, those who do not hope to meet Us, say: "Bring a different Qur'an, or make amendments to this one." Say: "It is not for me to change it of my will. I follow (only) what is revealed to me. If I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of an awful Day."
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers ask Prophet Muhammad to do with the Quran, and how did he respond?
ai.summary: In Surah Yunus, this verse highlights the core Shia theological principle of *Tawqif* (divine specification), emphasizing that the Prophet’s authority to convey the message is strictly limited to what is revealed, rejecting personal innovation (*Ra'y*). The disbelievers' challenge to 'alter' the Quran underscores the belief in its divine preservation, while the Prophet’s fear of the 'great Day' reflects the eschatological weight of faithful transmission. This narrative serves as a foundational proof for the infallibility of the Prophet in delivering the message without addition or subtraction.
